meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/343 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings

items.heading: CHAPTER 1

items.text: This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning:
items.heading: Article 1
items.comment: The presumption of innocence also appies to administrative punitive proceedings. In this sense, article 53.2 b) of Law 39/2015, of October 1, of the Common Administrative Procedure of Public Administrations provides that: In the case of administrative procedures of a sanctioning nature, the alleged perpetrators will have the following rights: (...) b) The presumption of non-existence of administrative liability until proven otherwise.

items.text:
(a)

certain aspects of the presumption of innocence in criminal proceedings;

(b)

the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings.

This Directive applies to natural persons who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. It applies at all stages of the criminal proceedings, from the moment when a person is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence, or an alleged criminal offence, until the decision on the final determination of whether that person has committed the criminal offence concerned has become definitive.
items.heading: Article 2

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Case Law recognizes the application of the right to the presumption of innocence as a rule of treatment throughout the criminal proceedings (SSTC 128/1995, 67/1997, 107/1997, 117/1998, 217/2001 or 185/2014; SSTS no. 277/2013 of February 13; No. 543/2015 of September 23; or No. 14/2018 of January 16). However, national legislation only refers to the presumption of innocence as a mandatory rule of judgment at the time of sentencing

items.heading: CHAPTER 2

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons are presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.
items.heading: Article 3

provisions.textEn: "Everyone has the right (...) to the presumption of innocence"

items.comment: Case law ensure this treatment for the accused person according to the general provision contained in the Spanish Constitution according to which "everyone has the right (...) to the presumption of innocence" (Article 24.2 Spanish Constitution)

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that, for as long as a suspect or an accused person has not been proved guilty according to law, public statements made by public authorities, and judicial decisions, other than those on guilt, do not refer to that person as being guilty. This shall be without prejudice to acts of the prosecution which aim to prove the guilt of the suspect or accused person, and to preliminary decisions of a procedural nature, which are taken by judicial or other competent authorities and which are based on suspicion or incriminating evidence.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
Data leaks during the investigation phase of the criminal procedure are punishable by law with a fine. In this sense the Article 301 LECrim states that "The investigative phase will be reserved and will not be public until the oral trial is opened, with the exceptions determined in this Law. The lawyer or solicitor of any of the parties who improperly disclose the contents of the summary will be corrected with a fine of 500 to 10,000 euros. Any other person who, not being a public official, commits the same offense shall incur the same fine. The civil servant, in the case of the preceding paragraphs, will incur the responsibility that the Criminal Code indicates".


Additionally, in cases of data leaks from criminal investigations in progress, criminal liability can emerge. In this sense, the crime of secret disclosure (articles 197 et seq. of the Criminal Code) may be applicable, which may lead to prison penalties.


However, as noted, these fines and penalties are not linked to violations of the presumption of innocence, but more generally to disclosures of reserved data of criminal investigations.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that appropriate measures are available in the event of a breach of the obligation laid down in paragraph 1 of this Article not to refer to suspects or accused persons as being guilty, in accordance with this Directive and, in particular, with Article 10.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 3. The obligation laid down in paragraph 1 not to refer to suspects or accused persons as being guilty shall not prevent public authorities from publicly disseminating information on the criminal proceedings where strictly necessary for reasons relating to the criminal investigation or to the public interest.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Presentation of suspects and accused persons

items.text: 1. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that suspects and accused persons are not presented as being guilty, in court or in public, through the use of measures of physical restraint.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
The article 520.1 LECrim states that arrest and provisional detention shall be conducted in the manner that least harms the person, reputation and assets of the charged person. Those who order the detention and those responsible for practicing it as well as subsequent transfers, shall ensure the constitutional rights to their honor, privacy and image, with respect to the fundamental right to freedom of information.

It is noted that this general provision does not refer to the presumption of innocence, but is aimed at protecting other fundamental rights. However, in the absence of express legal provision, it could be understood that not harming the honor of the accused means not presenting him/her as guilty before the public.

items.text: 2. Paragraph 1 shall not prevent Member States from applying measures of physical restraint that are required for case-specific reasons, relating to security or to the prevention of suspects or accused persons from absconding or from having contact with third persons.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.heading: Article 6

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that the burden of proof for establishing the guilt of suspects and accused persons is on the prosecution. This shall be without prejudice to any obligation on the judge or the competent court to seek both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence, and to the right of the defence to submit evidence in accordance with the applicable national law.

provisions.textEn: "Everyone has the right (...) to the presumption of innocence"

items.comment: The rule according to which the burden of proof for stablishing the guilt of the accused is on the prosecution is the main consequence of the right to the presumption of innocence recognized in article 24.2 of the Spanish Constitution which states that: "Everyone has the right (...) to the presumption of innocence"

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that any doubt as to the question of guilt is to benefit the suspect or accused person, including where the court assesses whether the person concerned should be acquitted.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
According to settled case-law, the principle of in dubio pro reo, according to which any doubt as to the question of guilt is to benefit the suspect or accused person, is excluded from the guarantee of the presumption of innocence. This has been settled since 1983 (STS of January 31, 1983 -RJ 1983 \ 76-, then followed by the SSTS of July 7, 1984 -RJ 1984 \ 3833-, May 3, 1985. RJ 1985 \ 2435, or December 15, 1988 -RJ 1988 \ 9516-, More recently, SSTS núm. 1425/2005 de 5 diciembre o 936/2006 de 10 octubre. recently, STS núm. 549/2018, de 13 de noviembre) where the distinction between the two principles was established on the grounds that the presumption of innocence was recognized in the Constitution and in dubio pro reo was just a "general legal principle", arguing that the first one refers to the objective existence or non-existence of sufficient inculpatory evidence while the second one involves a subjective problem of assessment of evidence.

The main consequence of that distinction is that, while the violation of the presumption of innocence can be reviewed in cassation befor the Supreme Court and under amparo remedy before the Constitucional Court, the violation of the principle in dubio pro reo, being a subjective issue, is not subject to appeal and allegations of non-application of the principle lack constitutional significance (Constitutional Tribunal Judgement 16/2000).

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Right to remain silent and right not to incriminate oneself

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have the right to remain silent in relation to the criminal offence that they are suspected or accused of having committed.

provisions.textEn: Everyone has the right to the ordinary Judge predetermined by law, to the defense and to the assistance of a lawyer, to be informed of the accusation made against them, to a public process without undue delay and with all guarantees, to use the relevant means of proof for their defense, not to testify against themselves, not to confess guilty and to the presumption of innocence.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Article 118. 1. Any person to whom a punishable act is attributed may exercise the right of defense (...) to which effect shall be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights: (...) g) The right to remain silent and not to give a statement if s/he does not wish to do so, and not to answer any or some of the questions asked.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have the right not to incriminate themselves.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Article 118. 1. Any person to whom a punishable act is attributed may exercise the right of defense (...) to which effect shall be instructed, without undue delay, of the following rights: (...) h) Right not to testify against oneself and not to confess guilt.

items.text: 3. The exercise of the right not to incriminate oneself shall not prevent the competent authorities from gathering evidence which may be lawfully obtained through the use of legal powers of compulsion and which has an existence independent of the will of the suspects or accused persons.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Case Law applies this rule, for intance, in cases of requirements on accounting documents, which has an existence independent of the will of the suspects because its possession is required by commercial laws. However, procedural legislation provides nothing expressly.

items.text: 4. Member States may allow their judicial authorities to take into account, when sentencing, cooperative behaviour of suspects and accused persons.

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 10/1995, de 23 de noviembre, del Código Penal

provisions.textEn: It is considered an extenuating circumstance the fact that the guilty party had proceeded, before knowing that the judicial procedure is directed against him/her, to confess the infraction to the authorities.

In cases against corporate defendants, it is considered as an extenuating circumstance to have collaborated in the investigation of the fact by providing evidence, at any moment of the process, that were new and decisive to clarify the criminal responsibilities arising from the facts.

items.text: 5. The exercise by suspects and accused persons of the right to remain silent or of the right not to incriminate oneself shall not be used against them and shall not be considered to be evidence that they have committed the criminal offence concerned.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: There is relevant case Law on the evidentiary value of the defendant's silence, stating that cannot be used as a proof of guilt. However, if there are sufficient indications against the accused, his silence may serve to confirm them. Legislation provides nothing expressly.

items.text: 6. This Article shall not preclude Member States from deciding that, with regard to minor offences, the conduct of the proceedings, or certain stages thereof, may take place in writing or without questioning of the suspect or accused person by the competent authorities in relation to the offence concerned, provided that this complies with the right to a fair trial.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The unjustified absence of the accused shall not suspend the conclusion or resolution of the trial, provided that it has been cited with the formalities prescribed in this Law, unless the Judge, ex officio or at the request of a party, deems the declaration of the latter necessary.

items.comment: In criminal proceedings for minor crimes, the possibility of holding the trial in the absence of the accused is provided for by law, provided that s/he has been properly summoned. Taking into account that these proceedings take place in unity of act, without a previous phase of investigation, the absence of the accused at trial implies that no declaration will be taken.

items.heading: CHAPTER 3
items.subHeading: RIGHT TO BE PRESENT AT THE TRIAL

items.heading: Article 8
items.subHeading: Right to be present at the trial

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have the right to be present at their trial.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The holding of the public trial requires the assistance of the accused and the defense lawyer. However, if there are several accused persons and some of them do not appear in the trial without a legitimate reason, the Judge or Court may decide, after hearing the parties, the continuation of the trial for the other accused persons.

items.comment: The presence of the accused at the trial is not only a right, but constitutes an obligation for the accused

items.text: 2. Member States may provide that a trial which can result in a decision on the guilt or innocence of a suspect or accused person can be held in his or her absence, provided that:

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
The cases in which the Spanish legal system allows prosecution in absentia are much more limited than those provided for in European legislation since they are limited to less serious crimes, which carry short sentences (e.g. Melloni case).


In fact, the trial in absentia is only allowed in cases of unjustified absence of the defendant who had been summoned personally, or at the address designated by him/her for that purpose, at the request of the Prosecutor and after hearing the defense lawyer, when the judge considers that there are sufficient elements for prosecution, when the requested penalty does not exceed two years of deprivation of liberty or, if it were of a different nature, when its duration does not exceed six years (Article 786 Criminal Procedural Law).


That higher level of guarantees provided for in the Spanish legal system was clearly seen in the Judgment of the Court (Grand Chamber), 26 February 2013. Stefano Melloni v Ministerio Fiscal, in which the CJEU determined that an EAW cannot be rejected by adding extra conditions provided for in national legislation, and not provided for in the Framework Decision on EAW.

items.text:
(a)

the suspect or accused person has been informed, in due time, of the trial and of the consequences of non-appearance; or

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text:
(b)

the suspect or accused person, having been informed of the trial, is represented by a mandated lawyer, who was appointed either by the suspect or accused person or by the State.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 3. A decision which has been taken in accordance with paragraph 2 may be enforced against the person concerned.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 4. Where Member States provide for the possibility of holding trials in the absence of suspects or accused persons but it is not possible to comply with the conditions laid down in paragraph 2 of this Article because a suspect or accused person cannot be located despite reasonable efforts having been made, Member States may provide that a decision can nevertheless be taken and enforced. In that case, Member States shall ensure that when suspects or accused persons are informed of the decision, in particular when they are apprehended, they are also informed of the possibility to challenge the decision and of the right to a new trial or to another legal remedy, in accordance with Article 9.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: At any time when the person who has been convicted in absentia in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 786 (1) appears, s/he will be informed of the conviction for the purpose of compliance. Upon notification of the sentence, s/he will be informed of his/her right to file the appeal referred to in the following section, indicating the deadline for it and the competent body.

The sentence handed down in absentia, whether or not it has been appealed, is liable to be challenged in annulment by the convicted person within the same period and with the same requirements and effects as those established in the appeal procedure. The period will be counted from the moment in which it is proven that the convicted person was aware of the sentence.

items.comment:
Spain does not provide for the possibility of holding trials in the absence os suspects or accused person when conditions laid down in article 8.2 of the Directive 2016/343 are met. Extra conditions are required.

Spanish regulation is much more demanding since, as previously mentioned, for crimes of more than two years in prison or more than six years of other penalties, prosecution in absentia is never allowed (ArtIcle 786 Criminal Procesural Act). Nonetheless, in cases of prosecution in absentia, the right to a new trial is always provided

items.text: 5. This Article shall be without prejudice to national rules that provide that the judge or the competent court can exclude a suspect or accused person temporarily from the trial where necessary in the interests of securing the proper conduct of the criminal proceedings, provided that the rights of the defence are complied with.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: When the defendant disrupts order with an inconvenient conduct and persists in such conduct despite the warnings of the Court President and the warning to expel him/her from the Chamber, the Court may decide to expell him/her for a certain time or for the rest of the sessions, continuing the trial in his/her absence.

items.text: 6. This Article shall be without prejudice to national rules that provide for proceedings or certain stages thereof to be conducted in writing, provided that this complies with the right to a fair trial.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
In relation to the procedure for minor offenses, the law provides that "If the defendant lives outside the demarcation of the Court, s/he will not have the obligation to attend the trial, and may make his/her statements in writting alleging what s/he deems appropriate in his/her defense, as well as empower a lawyer to represent him/her making allegations and presenting evidence" (Article 970).

For these proceedings, it is also provided that "The unjustified absence of the accused shall not suspend the trial, provided that the defendant has been summoned with the formalities prescribed in this Law, unless the Judge, ex officio or at the request of any party, considers his/her statement essential"(Article 971).

items.text: Member States shall ensure that, where suspects or accused persons were not present at their trial and the conditions laid down in Article 8(2) were not met, they have the right to a new trial, or to another legal remedy, which allows a fresh determination of the merits of the case, including examination of new evidence, and which may lead to the original decision being reversed. In that regard, Member States shall ensure that those suspects and accused persons have the right to be present, to participate effectively, in accordance with procedures under national law, and to exercise the rights of the defence.
items.heading: Article 9

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: At any time when the person who has been convicted in absentia in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 786 (1) appears, will be informed of the conviction for the purpose of compliance. Upon notification of the sentence, s/he will be informed of his/her right to file the appeal referred to in the following section, indicating the deadline for it and the competent body.

The sentence handed down in absentia, whether or not it has been appealed, is liable to be challenged in annulment by the convicted person within the same period and with the same requirements and effects as those established in the appeal procedure. The period will be counted from the moment in which it is proven that the convicted person was aware of the sentence.

items.heading: CHAPTER 4
Article 10

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have an effective remedy if their rights under this Directive are breached.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
The appeal must be based on any of the following reasons:


a) That in the procedure or in the judgment there has been a breach of the rules and procedural guarantees, which will cause defenselessness, if the timely claim for rectification has been made. This claim will not be necessary if the alleged violation involves the violation of a constitutionally guaranteed fundamental right.

(...)

e) That the right to the presumption of innocence was violated because, given the evidence practiced at the trial, the sentence imposed lacks any reasonable basis.

items.comment: In addition to the possible appeal, if the trial was held in absentia outside the cases provided for in the law or when the right to the presumption of innocence was violated, cassation appeal before the Supreme Court for violation of a constitutional provision and an application for amparo before the Constitutional Court would be available.

items.text: 2. Without prejudice to national rules and systems on the admissibility of evidence, Member States shall ensure that, in the assessment of statements made by suspects or accused persons or of evidence obtained in breach of the right to remain silent or the right not to incriminate oneself, the rights of the defence and the fairness of the proceedings are respected.

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial

provisions.textEn: Evidence obtained, directly or indirectly, violating the fundamental rights or freedoms will not take effect

items.comment: The rights not to incriminate oneself, to remain silent and the presumption of innocence are fundamental rights contained in the Article 24 (2) of the Spanish Constitution. In view of their consideration as fundamental rights, evidence obtained by violating them is null and void.
